sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Replication lag
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: causes include an undersized replica, 'long-running replica queries' that block replay, and an overloaded replica; metrics replica_lag and network_lag ('If network_lag is negligible but replica_lag is high, the replica is the bottleneck'); fixes: right-size the replica, tune max_standby_streaming_delay (about 30-60 seconds) and check pg_stat_database_conflicts, 'Use different replicas for OLTP and OLAP'. That promoting a replica stops replication for good is from memory of the 'Promote replicas' page (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the database engineer at Fennick Outdoor. The storefront reads stock levels from orders-db-replica1, a Cloud SQL read replica of orders-db. Since about 12:55 customers buy items shown in stock that sold out long ago. The replica's lag is 25 minutes and climbing. A limited-edition jacket drop goes live at 14:00.
handover: Finance's month-end report was pointed at the same replica last week 'to take load off the primary'.
orders-db-replica1 has max_standby_streaming_delay set to -1 (wait forever) from an old tuning.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the primary, the read replica that serves stock levels and what else runs on that replica.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the replica fell behind, what you changed, and how reads stay fresh.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: network_lag was 1 second but replica_lag climbed to 25 minutes: the replica received WAL and could not replay it. A 26-minute finance query held replay, and max_standby_streaming_delay -1 made the replica wait for it indefinitely.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Cancelled the finance query, set the delay to 30 seconds, and created a separate reporting replica. Promoting replica1 would have frozen it 25 minutes in the past.

parts.label: Fresh
parts.modelAnswer: OLTP reads and reporting are on different replicas, and lag over 30 seconds alerts.

frozen.headline: Promotion ends replication
frozen.body: A promoted replica is a separate database. Stale reads come from replay being blocked; unblock replay instead.

oversold.headline: Replica lag behind a reporting query
oversold.body: Long queries on a replica can block replay. Keep OLTP and OLAP on different replicas, and set max_standby_streaming_delay so replay is not held forever.

caughtUp.headline: Good: read the lag before acting
caughtUp.body: You told network lag from replay lag, found the query holding replay, unblocked it and capped the wait, gave reporting its own replica, checked stock, and alerted on lag.

scoring.modelReasoning: Network lag is a second while replica lag is 25 minutes, so the replica is not applying WAL. A long finance query on the same replica blocks replay, and the delay setting tells the replica to wait forever. Cancel the query, cap the standby delay, and give reporting its own replica; then alert on lag. Promoting the replica ends replication; more connections change nothing.
